PullRequest.Title: chat: Show installed plugin repository provenance
PullRequest.Body:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

## Summary

Installed plugin details currently lose marketplace source metadata that is available while browsing. This change preserves trustworthy GitHub repository provenance and surfaces it alongside the installed version and location.

- Projects repository metadata from configured plugin marketplaces into customization resources.
- Resolves installed provenance from direct marketplace metadata first, then the installation catalog association.
- Links canonical GitHub repositories from installed plugin details, targeting the validated ref and plugin path when available.
- Omits ambiguous, malformed, query-bearing, fragment-bearing, non-HTTPS, and non-GitHub repository values rather than inferring provenance.
- Refreshes only the repository row when asynchronous installation metadata arrives, preserving the user's current focus.
- Keeps the repository link shrink-wrapped so only its visible text is clickable, with truncation and custom hover behavior for constrained layouts.

Author and source-update timestamps are not exposed by the current authoritative marketplace contracts, so this change does not fabricate those fields. This PR does not add the author or last-updated metadata requested in #343866; that issue remains open and requires authoritative marketplace fields.

## How to Test

1. Open Chat Customizations and select an installed plugin from the GitHub Feed.
2. Confirm Details shows Version, a linked Repository, and Location.
3. Confirm only the visible repository text is clickable and opens the validated GitHub ref and plugin path when that source metadata is available.
4. Check a relative-path plugin from a configured GitHub marketplace and confirm the marketplace repository and plugin path are used when direct repository metadata is unavailable.
5. Check npm-, Python-, non-GitHub-, and otherwise untrusted sources and confirm no unrelated marketplace repository is presented as plugin provenance.

Scenarios.Scenario: Browse or search a configured plugin marketplace page
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing marketplace query must complete before results render; afterward up to the requested page size (default 30) is mapped synchronously. The diff adds repository URI normalization during that bounded mapping but no additional awaited work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing query per marketplace page request; the returned page defaults to at most 30 items.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same marketplace query occurred, and each returned item was mapped without the repository URI field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The query remains on the page-render critical path; added repository projection runs only after it returns.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Marketplace page size, default 30; one small URI/regex normalization per result.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One marketplace service query is awaited per provider page request; the added per-result normalization is synchronous and does not create concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Marketplace service caching behavior is unchanged. The diff neither adds nor bypasses a cache and does not alter cache keys or miss handling.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the provider call path and default page-size bound.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact marketplace response latency and user query frequency vary, but the added CPU/allocation is bounded by page size and contains no boundary call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: bounded linear projection adds only small URI parsing/allocation and no I/O, fan-out, or critical-path boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open an installed plugin detail and receive asynchronous installation metadata or plugin state updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial detail rendering reads the current in-memory installation snapshot and builds one repository row. Later observable updates resolve provenance and update only that row unless policy enablement requires an existing full rerender.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load the plugin README through the existing file/request services
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the existing README load for the single selected plugin and render generation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening the same detail already rendered and loaded the README.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: README loading is asynchronous and unchanged; repository resolution does not add or repeat this boundary during row-only metadata refreshes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the repository URI through the opener service after an explicit link click
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One opener invocation per explicit user click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no installed repository link to click.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the detail-render critical path and initiated only by the user.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected plugin. Snapshot findByTarget uses ResourceMap/Map indexes, so lookup does not scan the installation collection; provenance parsing scales only with short repository/ref/path strings.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Only one embedded plugin detail is active. Installation-provider refreshes are versioned/cancelled upstream and identical installation arrays are suppressed before the observable emits; repository row work itself is synchronous.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The service memoizes an indexed installation snapshot until an actual change invalidates it. Warm reads reuse the snapshot; cold rebuild behavior is pre-existing. No negative lookup retries or new cache lifecycle are introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the autorun, snapshot implementation, provider refresh deduplication, and disposable ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Repository/ref/path lengths and installation-change frequency vary, but effective cardinality remains one selected detail and indexed lookup.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: updates are bounded, indexed, and row-local; hover/listener resources are disposed on refresh, rerender, and detail disposal.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a marketplace resource detail with repository/source links
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The resource facts render synchronously. The diff registers delayed hover support for each rendered link; README fetching and installation state work remain unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing load for the selected resource/render generation when a README URI is present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same selected resource triggered the README load.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and not introduced or multiplied by hover registration.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open an external fact link after explicit user activation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One opener invocation per user click, unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Fact links already invoked openExternal; the diff only adds delayed hover UI.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: A small fixed number of fact links for one selected resource.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single selected marketplace detail is rendered; delayed hover creation does not start concurrent remote work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache, cache key, or negative-cache behavior changes. Delayed hover content is a local label string.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the render path and renderDisposables lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of facts varies by resource, but remains a small fixed detail set rather than a collection-scale path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added hover registrations are bounded to visible links and disposed on rerender/disposal, with no layout loop or expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all nine changed files and all diff pages. Traced marketplace-page projection, installed-detail observable refresh, repository link activation, hover lifecycles, snapshot indexing, upstream provider deduplication, and existing README boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.
